title: Cross platform paths and line endings in CLIs
when: A command line tool must behave the same on linux, mac and win32: paths, home folders, line endings, case sensitivity and launching other programs.
inputs: files the tool reads and writes
prompt:
Goal: Every path built with node:path, any line ending accepted on read, one chosen ending on write, and programs spawned without shell assumptions.
Steps:
1. Build paths with path.join and path.resolve, never by gluing "/"; module locations via fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), not new URL(...).pathname, which breaks on drive letters and spaces.
2. Home and temp: os.homedir() and os.tmpdir().
3. Show paths with path.relative(process.cwd(), p); compare after path.resolve, folding case on win32 and mac.
4. Globs and config values use forward slashes; convert with p.split(path.sep).join("/").
5. Read with text.split(/\r?\n/); write "\n" by default, or keep a file's own ending when editing in place (detect "\r\n" in the first line); offer --eol crlf.
6. .gitattributes: * text=auto eol=lf and *.cmd text eol=crlf; a CRLF shebang fails with "env: node\r".
7. Spawn with execFile or spawn and an args array; on win32 .cmd and .bat files need a shell, so launch Node scripts with process.execPath instead.
Quality bar:
- No hardcoded separators or drive letters.
- Tests run on all three systems in CI.
- Names with spaces and non ASCII letters work.
Pitfalls:
- path.join on URLs; use new URL(rel, base).
- Assuming a case sensitive file system.
- Reserved win32 names (con, nul, aux) as output files.
Verify:
- [ ] No concatenated paths.
- [ ] fileURLToPath for module paths.
- [ ] Reader accepts CRLF.
- [ ] .gitattributes present.
Output: src/paths.mjs, src/eol.mjs, .gitattributes and tests for both helpers.

examples.input: minha CLI funciona no linux mas quebra no windows
examples.output: src/paths.mjs with path.join and fileURLToPath, reader splitting on /\r?\n/, .gitattributes eol=lf, spawn with process.execPath
